newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Gov disputes $700 mln excess revenue forecast.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Gov disputes $700 mln excess revenue forecast.

text.p: New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman said Wednesday she does not agree with an estimate by the state's Office of Legislative Services that revenues for fiscal year 1997 will exceed projections by $700 million.
The governor told reporters at a press conference that state Treasurer Brian Clymer would certify just $450 million of excess revenues.
Tuesday, Clymer said revenues collected through April 30 were about $167 million over projections, with two months left before the fiscal year ends on June 30.
The Office of Legislative Services is the Legislature's non-partisan agency responsible for monitoring state budget and revenue trends.

Whitman also said at the press conference that she was disappointed with a state Supreme Court ruling Wednesday ordering the administration to funnel more money to poor school districts in the state. The ruling also supported Whitman's plan to institute core curriculum standards.

Whitman said she had no plans as yet to use the excess revenues to lower the budgetary effects of her proposed $2.8 billion pension bond deal, which includes provisions to save nearly $600 million for the budget.
